geometry.name: study_compass_256x256x1
geometry.provenance: The co-design study's COMPASS tile as the toolchain's core: 256 rows by 256 cells of 1 bit(s) hold 256 x 64 four-bit weights (a tile of R rows, C columns and b bits per cell holds R x C // ceil(4 / b) 4-bit weights, route (b)'s translation, e2e/driver/declarations.py); 576 tiles, the study's budget chip A_L (cd41_chip.A_L = 576 tiles; park2025compass Table I's L chip). The tile count is a study axis (the study's ladder cd_preview.CAPS, 144 to 1,152 tiles), declared per point through target_overrides with a note. has_bias: the study's census holds no bias row (x9_0_v3.census counts ceil(cin k^2 / R) rows), the bias enters at the output stage.

faithfulness.note: The chip of the study as its estimator prices it (codesign.md, constants.md, audit_v4/pd.md). Every departure is named in the rows and the description of the profile.

notes: The certified function applies one ADC (the run's readout law) to each column's fused accumulator, as on every lane bundle; the study's tile accumulates its 32-bit partial sums exactly and converts nothing, and its cost model prices no conversion (W47's per-array ADC is not built). allow_coalescing and allow_neuron_splitting are true: the study's census splits a layer's rows over ceil(cin k^2 / R) tiles and its columns over ceil(cout / 64) tiles, accumulating 32-bit full-precision partial sums (constants.md sec. 4, jiang2023a p.2-3). onchip_arithmetic declares the lane subset L, E and P on the ng45_os_lane block, one lane per 64 output columns (one per tile): the block the study's capability-on tile-area factor s_AU reads (arith_toggle.md sec. 6; codesign.md sec. 2.2, D136: 1.069 to 1.130 of a G3 tile, frozen picks at 1.130). The study prices no lane energy (about 0.4% of MAC energy); the toolchain prices the block's e_lane_op. activation_bits is not set: the study carries 8-bit activations at its cuts and prices a tile activation at 8 bit-serial cycles, while a program declares its own value grid.

unstated.note: The study's tile holds 64 four-bit weights per row in 65,536 bit cells (constants.md sec. 2): one bit per cell, four per weight, a count the study computes and does not state.
The study's tile states bit cells, not a number of bits per cell.
The study's census counts ceil(cin k^2 / R) rows per layer (x9_0_v3.py census), no bias row: the bias enters at the output stage, the description's assumption from the census.

The study prices 8-bit activations at its cuts (constants.md sec. 2: 'Activations. 8 bits at cuts'), a tile activation at 8 bit-serial cycles (cd41_chip.T_ACT); the tile takes any input width bit-serially, so the description leaves the activation grid to the program (the bundle's notes).

stated.location: RA/06_parts/constants.md sec. 4 'Digital SRAM-CIM macro rows', the jiang2023a row the study's tile prices
stated.quote: Exact accumulation (full-width digital adder trees) in every row. ... 8b W, 4b inputs, 32b full-precision partial sums (p2-3)

reads.output_law: Exact accumulation (full-width digital adder trees) in every row

assumed_fields.range: the toolchain's converter form (W34's point form): the range calibrated from data; the study converts nothing
assumed_fields.mult_bits: the toolchain's converter form (W34's point form): a 24-bit requantization multiplier; the study states no multiplier

stated.note: The study's tile accumulates its 32-bit partial sums exactly and converts nothing: the identity converter at 32 bits (route (b)'s READOUT_LAW_INT is this law).

unstated.note: The study prices a capability-on arm at the declared lane cost (codesign.md, the estimator convention, D136) and an off arm; the lanes L, E and P are the owner's ruling of 2026-10-15 (on by default for value-domain chips) on the ng45_os_lane block the study's s_AU reads.
The study's tiles hold static weights; no run-time writable matrix is declared.
